thread:
hannah: quick Q — we got a failed webhook from a partner, header x-request-ref: r-0a4b7c. where's the fastest place to pull the full request lines + any linked spans? console or CLI? customer is seeing errors right now.

ben: console is fastest for a quick triage: Observability → Requests, paste the header value in the search box. it surfaces the request doc with links to trace and raw logs when present. if you prefer CLI: try redwoodctl logs query (see snippet). :eyes:

maria: +1 to console for eyeballs. for automation / reproducible hunting, use this CLI pattern:

```
# query recent logs by header via CLI
redwoodctl logs query --filter "headers.x-request-ref='r-0a4b7c'" --json | jq '.entries[] | {ts, level, msg, req_id}'
```

ben: note: sometimes the request doc doesn't have a trace link. check for traceparent or correlation_id fields in the request payload/headers — the proxy may have stripped/added them. span_link is the field we try to populate.

maria: if you only have an internal request id (not the header) older services expose: `redwoodctl requests get <REQUEST_ID> --raw` which prints the stored request + any metadata.

hannah: thanks — i tried the console and it showed the request doc but no trace link. ran the CLI filter, got a few entries but still no span_link. what's the next step to join to traces?

alex: if there's no span_link, try the ingress proxy logs — they usually preserve trace headers. example (gcloud):

```
gcloud logging read 'resource.type="gce_instance" AND textPayload:("x-request-ref: r-0a4b7c")' --limit 50
```

maria: also look for structured fields: request.metadata.correlation_id or sometimes `corr_id` in older services. those can map to the trace.

ops-bot: NOTE: If you need a deeper historical search (retention >30d) contact #observability with the request id so we can run an on-demand scan.

hannah: got it — found an ingress line with a `traceparent` header; followed the trace in the Trace UI and spotted a bad downstream span (timeout) — PR submitted and fixed. thanks everyone :raised_hands:

ben: if anyone wants a one-liner to jump from a trace id to related log request ids, i use this helper in my local toolbox:

```
tracectl get-spans <TRACE_ID> --format json | jq -r '.spans[].attributes."logging.request_id"' | xargs -n1 -I{} redwoodctl logs get {}
```

maria: i'll drop a short doc in #docs-observability with these snippets + the exact console clicks. :memo: leaving notes about edge cases (no span_link, proxy header stripping).

hannah: perfect. closing loop — one perms note: redwoodctl needs the `observer` role to run some of these commands. i'll file an access request for the support team.

ben: nice work — glad it was quick to resolve. :thumbsup:
